name: cdac-bit-settling
description: Per-bit CDAC top-plate settling for the MCS/Vcm-based switching scheme chosen in DR-0006: four bit trials spanning the sub-array's weight range (w=1, 16, 64, 256), both switching directions at the predicted-worst weight, over the full PVT matrix.
claim: spec/cdac-sizing-memo.md#settling-and-reference-drive (pending #1 for a ratified spec anchor). Cross-checks DR-0002's Z_ref <= 240 ohm / C_dec >= 40 nF envelope against this scheme's real per-step behaviour.
analyses: tran 25p 500n 0 10p
meas tran vpre_w1 FIND v(vtop_w1) AT=0.5n
meas tran vearly_w1 FIND v(vtop_w1) AT=1.5n
meas tran v1msps_w1 FIND v(vtop_w1) AT=63.5n
meas tran v2msps_w1 FIND v(vtop_w1) AT=32.25n
meas tran vsettled_w1 FIND v(vtop_w1) AT=500n
meas tran vpre_w16 FIND v(vtop_w16) AT=0.5n
meas tran vearly_w16 FIND v(vtop_w16) AT=1.5n
meas tran v1msps_w16 FIND v(vtop_w16) AT=63.5n
meas tran v2msps_w16 FIND v(vtop_w16) AT=32.25n
meas tran vsettled_w16 FIND v(vtop_w16) AT=500n

err_1msps_w1_mv.description: THE BUDGET CHECK, w=1 (sub-array LSB trial). Top-plate settling error 62.5 ns after the bit trial begins (1 MS/s, M=16, see spec/prior-art-survey.md Sec 1.4). Bound is 0.5 LSB at the tightest (single-ended) LSB = 3.2227 mV, illustrative pending the ratified spec (#1). Note this trial's whole step IS 1 LSB, so the bound is half its own excursion -- not a formality.

err_1msps_w256u_mv.description: same budget check, w=256 (the derivation's predicted-worst trial), UP direction (Vcm -> V_ref). By 62.5 ns the circuit is many time constants settled at every corner (see lag_early_* for the corner-sensitivity anchor at a time still inside the transient), so this value legitimately reads at or near the simulator's numeric floor everywhere -- that IS the finding (huge settling margin), not a broken sweep.

err_1msps_w256d_mv.description: same budget check, w=256, DOWN direction (Vcm -> GND). Checked separately because the NMOS/PMOS T-gate legs are not symmetric (different W, different body-effect direction near each rail), so the two directions are not guaranteed to settle identically.

lag_early_w256u.description: CORNER-SENSITIVITY ANCHOR, not a budget check (no min/max bound): residual top-plate lag at 1.5 ns as a fraction of the trial's own step, still well inside the transient at every corner (unlike the 62.5/31.25 ns budget points, which are so thoroughly settled everywhere that they carry no exploitable spread -- the same reasoning sim/device-mismatch-mc/ uses for its own corner-invariant headline result). This is what proves both the MOS corners (switch R_on) and the MiM/MOS-cap corners (array C) are actually reached by this testbench; neither the mos nor the cdac corner set alone would exercise both, which is why the manifest uses the full corner set. Without this floor the testbench would pass with every model section forced to typical (sim/selftest.sh stage 4).

lag_ord_256_64.description: PER-BIT ORDERING CLAIM 1 of 3. The settling derivation in the testbench header predicts tau(w) proportional to Ceq(w) = w*(512-w)*C_u/512, maximised at w=256. Stated as a measurement: the w=256 trial must lag MORE at the common 1.5 ns probe than the w=64 trial, at every PVT point. A positive floor (rather than >= 0) is used so the assertion cannot be satisfied by two identical numbers -- which is what a broken instantiation (e.g. all four branches accidentally the same size) would produce.

lag_ord_64_16.description: PER-BIT ORDERING CLAIM 2 of 3: w=64 must lag more than w=16.

lag_ord_16_1.description: PER-BIT ORDERING CLAIM 3 of 3: w=16 must lag at least as much as w=1. The floor is 0 rather than positive here because w=1's time constant (Ceq = 17.2 fF against the switch R_on, tau ~ 10 ps) is two orders of magnitude below the 200 ps driving edge, so that trial is edge-rate-limited rather than RC-limited and its residual lag is legitimately zero to numeric precision at every corner. That is itself the finding: the LSB trial has no RC settling problem at all.

step_w1_mv.description: Realized charge-divider step for w=1: ideally (V_ref/2)*(1/512) = 3.2227 mV = exactly 1 LSB, moving +-10% with the supply. The process-axis CEILING is a real claim, not a formality: a die-global capacitance shift (mim_ff/mim_ss) cancels exactly in the C_step/(C_step+C_fixed) ratio, which is why a CDAC's linearity is set by LOCAL mismatch and not by the process corner -- and why the PDK's missing local-mismatch model (sim/device-characterization-report.md Sec 5.1) cannot be substituted for by a corner sweep. This ceiling would also pass under --sabotage-corners; lag_early_w256u's process FLOOR is what makes the sweep falsifiable.

step_w256u_mv.description: same, w=256 UP: ideally (V_ref/2)*(256/512) = 825 mV, i.e. 256 LSB -- the sub-array MSB trial moves the top plate by exactly its own weight in LSB, which is the arithmetic sanity check that the divider is wired as the scheme intends.

notes: err_2msps_* are computed (see measure block) and reported in this record for the 2 MS/s stretch, but carry NO `checks` bound: DR-0002 already flags the 2 MS/s stretch reference-drive model as unresolved, and this testbench's job is to report the real number against that open question, not to gate the (non-mandatory) stretch target.

Four of the nine switched bit trials are instantiated (w = 1, 16, 64, 256), spanning the sub-array's whole weight range. The claim under test is a monotonic bound, not nine independent numbers: the three lag_ord_* checks assert the ordering the tau(w) = R_on*w*(512-w)*C_u/512 derivation predicts, and the five omitted weights (2, 4, 8, 32, 128) lie strictly inside both the measured weight range and the measured lag envelope. This is why w=256 can be quoted downstream as the worst-case bit: it is measured to be, not assumed to be.

Switch sizing (NMOS W=10um, PMOS W=20um, L=0.28um) matches sim/device-switch-ron/ and sim/device-switch-charge-injection/ exactly, so this testbench's R_on inherits their measured PVT behaviour (worst case 570 ohm at ss_125c_2.97v) rather than an assumed placeholder. This is a conservative simplification carried from spec/prior-art-survey.md Sec 1.4's own convention: a real implementation would likely size the bottom-plate driver larger for a 256-unit block than for a single unit, which would only improve on the numbers reported here.

Each weighted block is ONE lumped mim_cap_2f0 device sized by capacitance value (via the measured density law in sim/device-characterization-report.md Sec 1.2), not w literally-instantiated unit devices. The settling physics this testbench measures depends only on total capacitance, not on how many discrete units compose it. Unit-to-unit matching is a separate question and is NOT answered here -- it is answered in spec/cdac-sizing-memo.md Sec 2-3 from a derated literature assumption, because the PDK has no local capacitor mismatch model at all (sim/device-characterization-report.md Sec 5.1).
